frequency_question: How often do sovereign debt managers successfully scale newly introduced structural intervention programs past their initial sizing tiers within their establishment windows?
membership_rule: Includes formalized, recurring central bank or treasury purchase/sale programs designed for structural liquidity or debt management rather than emergency crisis backstops, established since 1980.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Large-Scale Asset Purchase (LSAP / Quantitative Easing 1 initiation)
Bank of Japan Rinban (JGB purchase) programmatic volume expansion

coverage_note: 3 named; representative of major sovereign structural debt intervention scaling episodes
known_gaps: Excludes minor emerging market tweaks and purely temporary pandemic emergency measures.
skeleton: Three distinct structural debt intervention epochs across major economies where initial sizing was subsequently scaled up or capped based on issuance needs.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major comparable episodes
validity_reason: Sovereign debt management frameworks and institutional scaling behaviors evolve slowly over multi-decade debt regimes.
